facts.text: Cullen was founded in 1886 as a lumber company town by the Cullen Lumber Company, part of Louisiana's late 19th-century timber boom.
The town hosts a Kansas City Southern Railroad museum right across from the International Paper Company container plant, preserving its rail heritage.
In 1935, International Paper Company opened a mill in Cullen, becoming a major employer and anchoring the town's economy for decades.
Cullen was officially incorporated on June 16, 1955, under the Lawrason Act, transitioning from an unincorporated settlement to a formal municipality.
The town’s origins trace back to the region’s abundant virgin pine forests, which drew out-of-state investors and laborers to establish mills and support settlements.
